one_liner: Hospitalization or death by day 28: {{n:fin_nmv}} with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir vs {{n:fin_pbo}} with placebo ({{n:rrr}} relative risk reduction).
one_liner_plain: Nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir cut Covid-19 hospitalization or death by about 89% in high-risk outpatients

citation.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir for High-Risk, Nonhospitalized Adults with Covid-19
citation.authors: Hammond J, Leister-Tebbe H, Gardner A, et al.

sections.background: By late 2021, outpatients at high risk of severe Covid-19 had few good options: monoclonal antibodies had to be given by infusion or injection in a health care setting and could lose activity against new variants. Nirmatrelvir is an oral inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) with broad activity against human coronaviruses in the lab. It is paired with low-dose ritonavir, a pharmacokinetic enhancer that keeps nirmatrelvir levels up. EPIC-HR tested whether a 5-day oral course could keep high-risk patients out of hospital.

methods.design: Phase 2-3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (1:1) across sites in the United States, Europe, Latin America, Africa, and Asia.
methods.population: Symptomatic, unvaccinated, nonhospitalized adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, symptom onset no more than 5 days before randomization, and at least one risk factor for progression to severe Covid-19. {{n:n_total}} underwent randomization ({{n:n_nmv}} nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir, {{n:n_pbo}} placebo).
methods.intervention: Nirmatrelvir 300 mg plus ritonavir 100 mg by mouth every 12 hours for 5 days.
methods.comparator: Matching placebo every 12 hours for 5 days.
methods.primary_endpoint: Covid-19-related hospitalization or death from any cause through day 28, in patients treated within 3 days of symptom onset who had not received and were not expected to receive monoclonal antibodies (modified intention-to-treat population).
methods.follow-up: Efficacy through day 28; safety information collected through day 34.

sections.results: In the final primary analysis (treatment within 3 days of symptoms), {{n:fin_nmv}} of the nirmatrelvir group versus {{n:fin_pbo}} of the placebo group were hospitalized for Covid-19 or died through day 28: a difference of {{n:diff}} (95% CI −7.78 to −3.84; P<0.001) and a {{n:rrr}} relative risk reduction. The effect held at every look: the interim analysis showed {{n:int_nmv}} versus {{n:int_pbo}} ({{n:int_rrr}} relative risk reduction), and patients who started within 5 days had {{n:d5_nmv}} versus {{n:d5_pbo}} ({{n:d5_rrr}} relative risk reduction). Across the trial there were {{n:death_nmv}} deaths with nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir and {{n:death_pbo}} with placebo. Viral load at day 5 was lower with nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir (adjusted mean difference {{n:vl}} when started within 3 days). Treatment-emergent adverse events were similar overall ({{n:ae_nmv}} vs {{n:ae_pbo}}), serious adverse events were less common ({{n:sae_nmv}} vs {{n:sae_pbo}}), and dysgeusia ({{n:dys_nmv}} vs {{n:dys_pbo}}) and diarrhea ({{n:dia_nmv}} vs {{n:dia_pbo}}) were more frequent with the active drug.
sections.conclusions: Treating symptomatic, high-risk, unvaccinated outpatients with nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir lowered the risk of progression to severe Covid-19 by 89% compared with placebo, without evident safety concerns. The benefit held whether treatment started within 3 days or within 5 days of symptoms.
sections.limitations: The trial enrolled only unvaccinated people (vaccinated high-risk patients were studied separately in EPIC-SR), and recruitment ended on December 9, 2021, so the absolute benefit in today's mostly vaccinated or previously infected patients may be smaller. Ritonavir carries important drug interactions: nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir is contraindicated with certain drugs because of the risk of serious adverse events, and others need dose adjustment or a pause.
sections.practice_impact: EPIC-HR made oral nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir a first-line treatment for high-risk outpatients with mild-to-moderate Covid-19, started as early as possible and within 5 days of symptoms. It moved early treatment from infusion chairs to a pharmacy pickup, with a drug-interaction check as the key safety step.
